# Adjusted PIT-Wasserstein: A Calibration Metric for Probabilistic Estimators

A dispersion calibration metric for probabilistic estimators,
disentangled from bias and sharpness. Originally published as
Supplementary Appendix 2 of **Challen & Danon (2025), “Instantaneous
Reproduction Number Estimation From Modelled Incidence”**; this
repository is the extension into a standalone paper.

The [Lean proof
library](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/proof/README.md) gives
the asymptotic null laws for all three tests and instructions for
importing them into another Lean project.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Core concepts

The paper defines three metrics for assessing probabilistic estimators
and differentiating between, bias, dispersion miscalibration, and
skill-spread decoupling.

### Baseline PIT-Wasserstein (\\B\_{pit}\\)

\\B\_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum\_{i=1}^n{\|u_i - rank_i\|}\\

Where \\rank_i = (i-0.5)/n\\ and \\u_i\\ are the PIT values.

- **Range:** \[0, 0.5\]. Zero = perfect calibration and zero bias.
- **Property:** Symmetric on log-calibration for a given bias.
- **Validated:** Dependent on bias, dispersion calibration and sharpness
  in simulation.

### Adjusted PIT-Wasserstein (\\U^\*\_{pit}\\)

\\U\_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum\_{i=1}^n{\|u\_{i,adj} - rank_i\|}\\

Where \\rank_i = (i-0.5)/n\\ and \\u\_{i,adj}\\ are the bias-adjusted
PIT values.

- **Range:** \[0, 0.5\]. Zero = perfect calibration.
- **Property:** Symmetric on log-calibration — conservative and
  overconfident estimators of equal magnitude score equally.
- **Validated:** Independent of bias and sharpness in simulation.

### Directed PIT-Wasserstein (\\D^\*\_{pit}\\)

\\D\_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum\_{i=1}^n{(rank_i - u\_{i,adj}) \times
\operatorname{sgn}(0.5-rank_i)}\\

- **Range:** \[-0.25, +0.25\]
- **Direction:** Positive = overconfident (U-shaped PIT histogram);
  Negative = conservative (dome-shaped).

All three metrics have significance tests based on large-sample
reference distributions for independent PIT values. The adjusted tests
use reference laws derived for the Gaussian location model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Literature context

Closest existing work; all of it is in the `pit-wasserstein` Zotero
collection, and `references/literature-review.md` has the detail.

| Paper | Metric | Difference from \\U^\*\_{pit}\\ |
|----|----|----|
| **Wessel et al. (2025)** arXiv:2506.13687 | **MCB** = mean \|sorted PIT - uniform\| | No bias adjustment. Used as regularisation during training, not evaluation. |
| **Wilks (2018)** QJRMS 144:76–88 | Miscalibration penalty (deviations of PIT from uniform) | First PIT-uniformity penalty. Qualitative/binned, not Wasserstein. |
| **Kuleshov, Fenner & Ermon (2018)** ICML | PCE = sup-norm \|PIT CDF - uniform CDF\| | Sup-norm (KS-style), not L1/Wasserstein. No bias adjustment. |
| **Dheur & Ben Taieb (2023)** ICML | PCE (same definition) | Large-scale empirical study of PCE. |
| **Gneiting, Balabdaoui & Raftery (2007)** JRSS-B | — | Canonical PIT/calibration/sharpness framework. |
| **Hamill (2001)** MWR 129:550–560 | — | Rank histograms for ensemble verification. |
| **Brockwell (2007)** Stat. Prob. Lett. | — | Universal residuals / PIT residuals. |
| **Podsztavek et al. (2024)** ESANN | — | ML classification of PIT histogram shapes. |
| **Arrieta-Ibarra et al. (2022)** JMLR 23 | — | Survey of calibration metrics; reliability diagrams. |
| **Panaretos & Zemel (2019)** Annu. Rev. Stat. Appl. | — | Wasserstein distances in statistics. |
| **Bosse et al. (2024)** arXiv:2205.07090 | — | `scoringutils` has the AD test for PIT uniformity, no Wasserstein calibration metric. |

### Summary

The **adjusted PIT-Wasserstein (\\U^\*\_{pit}\\)** combines:

1.  **Bias adjustment** before PIT uniformity assessment (no other
    metric does this)
2.  **Wasserstein/L1 distance** rather than sup-norm (PCE) or binning
    (reliability diagrams)
3.  **Signed direction** (\\D^\*\_{pit}\\) distinguishing overconfidence
    from over-conservatism
4.  **Validation** showing it is independent of bias and sharpness

The closest existing metrics (Wessel et al.’s MCB, Kuleshov et al.’s
PCE) measure raw PIT uniformity without de-biasing, so represent
calibration as both bias and dispersion calibration and are not
informative on dispersion miscalibration in the presence of bias.

# Package index

## PIT-W scoring

- [`crps_fn_generator()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/crps_fn_generator.md)
  : Generate a CRPS calculating function based on a parametrised
  distribution name
- [`pit_w()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/pit_w.md)
  : Calculate a pit-wasserstein value for a single estimator
- [`prediction_scores()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/prediction_scores.md)
  : Score a parametrised probability distribution

## Significance tests

- [`b_pit_significance()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/b_pit_significance.md)
  : Significance test for the baseline PIT-Wasserstein metric
- [`d_pit_significance()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/d_pit_significance.md)
  : Significance test for the directed PIT-Wasserstein metric
- [`p_l1_bridge()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/p_l1_bridge.md)
  [`q_l1_bridge()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/p_l1_bridge.md)
  : Distribution of the L1 norm of the Brownian bridge
- [`u_pit_significance()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/u_pit_significance.md)
  : Significance test for the bias-adjusted undirected PIT-Wasserstein
  metric

## Simulations

- [`calibrated_locations()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/calibrated_locations.md)
  : Uniform predictions for testing
- [`calibrated_locations_general()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/calibrated_locations_general.md)
  : Uniform predictions for testing (general)
- [`configuration_plot()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/configuration_plot.md)
  : Produce a summary plot of a experimental configuration.
- [`generate_simulation()`](https://ai4ci.github.io/pit-wasserstein/reference/generate_simulation.md)
  : Generate an set of scenarios for testing scoring
